elements.scope_reason: Three parts: watery diarrhoea, cholera outbreak exposure within 5 days, cholera likely (probable rule)
elements.problem: Time direction is wrong. The rule has (<= (onset <exposure>) (time_ago 5 days)); per the house briefing (<= onset (time_ago N)) means onset was at least N days ago, whereas the page says exposure within the past 5 days, which needs (< onset (time_ago 5 days)). As written the rule fires only for exposure 5+ days ago and never for the recent exposure, so cholera (and the Urgent priority that depends on active Cholera) misfires. Also 'with or without vomiting' makes the nausea/vomiting conjunct in the rule harmful: a patient with watery diarrhoea and exposure but no nausea/vomiting does not get probable cholera (though the urgent trigger itself requires N/V so the effect is limited to the diagnosis).  Exposure as 'Exposure to (contextual qualifier)' + Vibrio cholerae is a reasonable stand-in for 'in cholera outbreak area'.
evidence: Diagnose probable cholera in nausea/vomiting :: (<= (onset (finding (snomed_concept "Exposure to (contextual qualifier)" "qualifier value") (snomed_concept "Vibrio cholerae" "organism"))) (time_ago 5 days))
(and (or nausea vomiting) (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Diarrhea" "finding") (qualifier (snomed_concept "Watery" "qualifier value"))) ...)

elements.scope_reason: 'Dyspepsia likely' and 'GORD likely' if BMI >= 25 and waist >= 80 (woman) / >= 94 (man); Hb referral thresholds not_representable
elements.problem: GORD rule applies waist >= 80 cm to everyone. For men the page requires >= 94, so men with waist 80-93 cm and BMI >= 25 are wrongly given probable GORD. Sex-specific thresholds should be split or flagged if sex cannot be expressed. Dyspepsia concept 'Indigestion' fine. Discuss/refer red flags (Hb, melaena, dysphagia etc.) are management/referral and not encoded (Hb not representable).

(>= (measurement (snomed_concept "Body mass index" "observable entity") kg/m²) 25)

rule_level_problems.problem: (<= onset (time_ago 5 days)) means exposure at least 5 days ago; page means within past 5 days, requiring (<). Cholera never fires for recent exposure, and Urgent via active Cholera is lost.

Requires nausea/vomiting although the page says watery diarrhoea 'with or without vomiting'.

Fires on any nausea/vomiting; page only says 'Exclude pregnancy' (a check), so it is a catch-all possible diagnosis.

rule_level_problems.rule: Check for causes of nausea/vomiting not needing urgent attention
rule_level_problems.problem: The check list covers gastroenteritis/dyspepsia/dehydration items but dehydration-leading check items are fine; no check_for for 'recent vomiting' pregnancy/medication/alcohol (management/cross-refs, acceptable).

summary: Most consequential: the cholera exposure time comparison is inverted ((<= onset (time_ago 5 days)) means 5+ days ago, page means within 5 days), so cholera and its Urgent trigger do not fire as intended. Second, GORD uses waist >= 80 cm for everyone though men need >= 94. Remaining red-box urgent criteria are encoded with reasonable SNOMED concepts, with minor approximations (no stools or flatus, purple/red rash, shock footnote).
